texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Museum of Farnham is  located in Willmer House, an  18th-century  town  house  completed  in  1718  with  a decorative brickwork façade on West Street in Farnham in Surrey. [1]   Events  were  held  in  2018  by  the  museum  to celebrate  the  300th  anniversary  of  the  building. [2]   The Museum houses a collection of artefacts spanning several periods  of  the  town's  history  and  prehistory.  Open  from Monday to Saturday, there is no admission charge. [3]  The Museum has  a  Muniment  Room  available  to  researchers with its extensive collection of printed material relating to Farnham and the surrounding area.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The museum was founded in 1961 to provide the Farnham community with a collection dedicated to the history of the local area in an elegant Grade I listed Georgian townhouse [1]   which  still  retains  many  original  features, including  a  walled  garden.  Spread  over  two  floors  and  in six rooms, displays include items from a large and eclectic collection; from ancient archaeological artefacts to nationally  important  artworks  by  local  artists  and  an extensive costume collection. [3] Permanent displays include an elaborately embroidered nightcap belonging to Charles I, who in 1649 stayed in a nearby house on his way to trial in London; [4]  a decorated and gilded cassone panel by W. H. Allen; artworks of local scenes by John Verney, [5] and objects connected with William Cobbett.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The Museum of Farnham is part of the Farnham Maltings Association,  a  creative  organisation  working  with  artists and  communities  to  encourage  people  to  get  involved  in Art  in  every  aspect,  including  making  and  seeing  Art.  To achieve that aim, the Museum is closely involved with the Farnham Maltings. [6]

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Wilmer House was purchased by Waverley Borough Council  from  Surrey  County  Council  in  2012. [7]   The  new owners began a £92,000 restoration of the façade but this was halted in 2017 when the condition was found to be much worse than thought. [8]  The council was notified that significant repair work was required in 2018 and since then scaffolding has been erected to protect the public from any falling masonry, this has partially obscured the façade. [8][7][9]

annotations.text: The image shows the Wikipedia logo with a blue puzzle piece on the right side and the text "25 years of the free encyclopedia" in smaller font below it.
The building in the image is a classic example of Georgian architecture, characterized by its symmetrical shape, brick facade, and white-framed windows with sashes.
A large, embroidered hat with a floral pattern in shades of blue and pink sits on a clear glass stand.
The image shows a section of a large, ornate panel with intricate gold leaf and detailed patterns, possibly part of a historical or religious structure.

The image shows an interior space resembling a dining room with a large round table set for four, surrounded by chairs, and features dark wood paneling on the walls, a fireplace with a mantelpiece above it, and various framed artworks and decorative items.
The image shows an interior space with three display cases on the left side, each containing various items and informational materials.
